$comment: Violet Hour Light palette -- the ONE place light colors are defined. Edit a hex, then `npm run build`. Solved against the same contrast budget as the dark variant; see scripts/contrast-check.js.

$design.concept: The violet hour seen from the other side: dawn rather than dusk. An off-white ground with a violet cast (never #FFFFFF, which glares), the same hue plan as the dark variant, every colour darkened until it clears the budget on a bright ground.
$design.notLightenedDark: A light theme is not an inverted dark theme. The binding constraints flip: the neutral ramp DESCENDS from the editor, edges are solved against the DARKEST adjacent surface rather than the lightest, and the luminance rule becomes a floor - nothing may be lighter than the body text.

hues.neutrals: 261-272 violet, saturation eased from 0.34 down to 0.25 as surfaces lighten so chrome never turns lurid
hues.identity: 262 lavender -- accent, focus, links, function names
hues.coolSky: 136 green (regex, attributes), 156 mint (template punctuation), 172 aqua (types AND intrinsic tags - deliberately one colour, an intrinsic element is a type-like thing), 206 sky (properties, git-modified)
hues.cssPlan: selector 46 gold, property 206 sky, value-keyword 156 mint, unit/number 14 coral - four well-separated hues, so no two frequent CSS tokens blur
